game.trade.help.body: Sign a trade agreement lasting {{day}} days; it can be renewed before it expires. Each day, receive [[funds:{{funds}}]] from your trade partner under the agreement. If you are an overlord, you provide this funding to your vassal instead. The agreement expires automatically.
game.vassal.help.body: Annex a vassal when your military, economic, and territorial strength leads enough, for [[politics:{{cost}}]]. Vassals assist their overlord with morale and armaments, while the overlord covers the vassal's military upkeep. A vassal declares independence once its overlord reaches the vassal limit.
game.alliance.help.body: Form a mutual defense alliance with another nation. Forming or breaking an alliance costs [[politics:{{cost}}]]. Allies cannot be targeted by declarations of war.
game.ai.tendency.aggressive.name: Aggressive Expansion
game.ai.tendency.aggressive.blurb: Prioritize building up the military and actively wage war.
game.ai.tendency.aggressive.trait: Mobilize often and sustain the war through conquest.
game.ai.tendency.economic.name: Economy First
game.ai.tendency.economic.blurb: Prioritize production and favor trade and vassals.
game.ai.tendency.balanced.name: Balanced Development
game.ai.tendency.balanced.blurb: Balance military and economy, adapting strategy to the situation.
game.ai.tendency.balanced.trait: Expand flexibly according to the situation.
game.ai.tendency.help.body:
AI nations adjust military, production, diplomacy, and deployment decisions by tendency.
- Aggressive Expansion: mobilize often and sustain the war through conquest.
- Economy First: grow steadily and expand cautiously.
- Balanced Development: expand flexibly according to the situation.

game.tendency.pacifist.name: Pacifist
game.tendency.pacifist.blurb: Focuses on domestic affairs and the economy, avoids starting wars, and mobilizes the whole nation only when invaded.
game.tendency.defensive.name: Defensive
game.tendency.defensive.blurb: Invests in border fortifications and garrison troops, seeks no expansion, but strikes back hard at any invasion.
game.tendency.bully.name: Bully
game.tendency.bully.blurb: Only attacks neighbors clearly weaker than itself; backs down, allies or stalls against strong powers.
game.tendency.opportunist.name: Opportunist Expansion
game.tendency.opportunist.blurb: Has no fixed enemies and seizes territory when neighbors are torn by unrest, defeated or economically collapsed.
game.tendency.hegemon.name: Hegemon
game.tendency.hegemon.blurb: Aims at regional hegemony, builds up the military and suppresses potential challengers without missing an expansion chance.
game.tendency.trader.name: Trading Nation
game.tendency.trader.blurb: Focuses on trade routes and ports, protects trade lines with military force, and is deeply hostile to those who blockade them.
game.tendency.ideologue.name: Ideological Export
game.tendency.ideologue.blurb: Intervenes in other nations' internal affairs, backs like-minded factions, and often fights to topple rival regimes.
game.tendency.isolated.name: Fortress Mentality
game.tendency.isolated.blurb: Neither allies, expands nor intervenes; fortifies its borders heavily and stays armed and neutral.
game.tendency.militarist.name: Militarist
game.tendency.militarist.blurb: Runs the state around war, prefers preemption and quick decisive battles, and has little patience for peace.

game.alliance.help.create: An alliance camp is founded by a leader for 40 political power, then like-minded nations are invited to join.
game.alliance.help.members: Members share military access and treat each other's enemies as common enemies: when any member goes to war or is attacked, the others join the same war.
game.alliance.help.invite: An invitation requires a shared enemy, or matching expansionist/defensive tendencies with sufficient diplomatic willingness. Isolationist nations never found alliances and rarely accept invitations.
game.alliance.help.cooldown: After the player rejects an alliance invitation, no further invitations or applications to the same alliance are possible for [[turn:5]].

game.trade.help.agreement: Trade agreements have a monthly and a fixed part: the monthly part is delivered automatically each turn, with its duration adjustable when proposed (20 turns by default); the fixed part is delivered once at signing.
game.trade.help.exchange: Resource exchange: both sides offer raw materials, food, industry or strategic resources; funds, manpower and political power are excluded.
game.trade.help.purchase: Purchase: we pay cash for any of those four resources. Mercenaries: we pay cash and the other side provides manpower only.
game.trade.help.aid: Aid request: we offer no consideration and may only ask for raw materials, food, industry or strategic resources; nations at war, destroyed, or refusing do not trade.
game.trade.help.ai: The AI checks its own stock and daily net growth; it always refuses when negative growth cannot be covered by stock, or when it is at war with the proposer.
game.trade.help.cooldown: Once confirmed, the proposal is sent immediately and answered next turn; after a refusal, the same kind of proposal cannot be sent to that nation again for [[turn:5]].

game.vassal.profile.cooperative.name: Cooperative
game.vassal.profile.cooperative.blurb: Pays an adjustable share of [[funds]] and [[industry]] in exchange for protection and [[politics]]; independence cap 300.
game.vassal.profile.autonomous.name: Autonomous
game.vassal.profile.autonomous.blurb: Pays only [[politics]] while the overlord provides protection; economy stays autonomous, independence cap 100.
game.vassal.profile.oppressive.name: Oppressive
game.vassal.profile.oppressive.blurb: Imposed by a peace settlement after defeat: pays [[politics]] and a fixed share of [[funds]], independence cap 500, most prone to rebellion.
game.vassal.help.territory: Vassals share their overlord's territory background colour and differ only by flag emblem; the overlord has military access to every vassal type, and vassals may enter overlord territory.
game.vassal.help.independence: Independence is the only vassal status value: it rises passively over time and from tribute that benefits the overlord, and falls from the overlord's protection and gifts. Autonomous cap 100, cooperative 300, oppressive 500; at 80% it is high and defection or revolt becomes likely; at the cap autonomous/cooperative vassals leave peacefully while oppressive ones rebel.
game.vassal.help.war: A vassal's entry into war depends on its tendencies: aggressive or expansionist vassals willingly answer an overlord's offensive war, while defensively minded ones are reluctant when the overlord strikes first. Vassals are more willing to help when the overlord is the victim of aggression. Oppressive vassals join every overlord war unconditionally; the player receives a pending call when acting as a vassal.
game.vassal.help.defection: Turnaround: bully, opportunist and expansionist vassals seek outside help for independence when their overlord looks weak and the attacker is strong, especially oppressive vassals; autonomous and cooperative vassals are less rebellious. High independence makes this more likely.
game.vassal.help.upgrade: Contract improvement: once independence reaches 60% of the cap, the nation's tendency is willing, and [[politics:{{cost}}]] has been saved, the vassal may ask the overlord to improve its contract (oppressive to cooperative, cooperative to autonomous); the overlord may refuse.
game.vassal.help.request: Weak nations may voluntarily request vassalage (the oppressive type cannot be chosen voluntarily); an overlord may also demand it. Once a vassal is selected, its tribute rate and contract type can be adjusted through diplomatic actions.
